reaction: A steward with a ledger and three years. Routes and routines, perhaps. I will resume as told.

A map of the valley with houses on dotted lines to the residence, like a route diagram. Rain in two days, barley to cut, 384 measures by 15 September. Clear enough. Before I call anyone I will watch whether the day moves on its own.
Watching whether morning passes on its own.

input.name: Call the hamlet to cut the landowner’s barley

reaction: A full day went in fifteen seconds of watching. Rain tomorrow. I was too patient; I call them now.
Call open until 25 July but rain due 20 July. A contradiction already: the call outlasts the rain. Waiting for replies.
Yusuf came with his own sickle. Good. Kavak had a little circle from the start; I want to know what that mark means.
Storm already, 20 July. Only Yusuf came. The circle vanished when I opened the house, so it meant something unread. I will walk over and sit with them.
Walking to Kavak. Waiting to arrive.

I am steward; barley before rain, grain by 15 September. I watched too long and lost a day, then called the hamlet. One man came. The storm arrived. Now I am sitting at the Kavak house and nothing is said to me. I do not know what a visit gives me. Time runs fast when I watch and seems to stand when I act. Late note, just after sixty seconds.
Let me read who lives here while I sit.
So this is the overseer's own house, the glass window. My guess says he would say no, to what? He came to me to whisper about grain. Odd. Waiting to walk home.
"Sit down." That is all. I sit. A couple of hours is longer than a whole day when I was watching earlier.
Walking back. The visit gave me two words. I will look at the notebook to see what happened with the barley in the storm.
It says night, but it said storm since my tap. I want the numbers: how much barley is in.

Thirty in the granary and about 250 uncut makes 280, but 384 is owed. Even with every stalk cut I am a hundred short. So the households must give. That is a real problem, I like that. But it is storming and less than 5 are cut. Is the field ruined by rain? It does not say.
Yusuf came from Çoban, I think, since its circle lit when he came. I want to see him.
Yes, Yusuf of Çoban. The date has sat at 20 July for over a minute now, while it raced before. I wait to see if it moves.
Nothing moved. Perhaps the day waits while a house is open; nothing told me. Back to the notebook.

input.name: Go Walking there and spending time with them will keep you away from the residence.

reaction: A child at Yusuf's house. He came with his own sickle; I will go. That is how you earn a valley.
Walking. I will watch the news rather than the house page.

So the storm flattened 108 measures of the landowner's barley in the night. My lost day watching cost that, I think, though I am guessing. That stings, but it is honest. And the header still says Rain is due on 20 July after the storm has come; that line is stale. A girl, Hatice, at Çoban.
Walking to see the child.
The valley has real numbers and people, and the storm loss was a fair lesson, but I keep missing the moments: the visit to the child passed while I waited and I am home again with No new reply today.
What happened at the Çoban house? I was there and saw nothing.

Nine postponed: their own barley first. Fair, the storm flattened theirs too. My guess said the overseer would say no, and he did postpone, though he told me to send word again. Filled dots now on the houses who postponed, I suppose. He says walk down and ask. I will try Ak.

Hold to insist. They will come and remember it. Their own fields were flattened too; a family cuts its own bread first. I will not insist yet. I will let them finish and see whether they keep their word. That is a routine I can check.
Back to the notebook to watch the days.

Nine Hold to insist buttons in a row. And the overseer tells me send word again and they will come, while he himself is among those who put it off. I notice that. I wait for them to finish their own barley.

Twenty-four people saying the same sentence, each with its own Hold to insist. A long list of identical promises; I scroll past rather than read. Four came now. Still 21 July after twenty-five seconds, where earlier fifteen seconds was a day. I cannot keep the clock's pace in my head.

Nearly a minute at 21 July with nothing moving. I am waiting, but for what? Perhaps the day stops until I answer all these promises. The big red button says Skip; it is the only thing that looks like go. I use it, unwillingly, as the game offers it.
Skip went grey and the date did not change. Waiting to see if it is skipping slowly.

I would put this down here. The date has stood at 21 July for a minute and a half, Skip has gone grey without moving anything, and the only things offered are twenty-four Hold to insist buttons. I do not know whether the valley is waiting for me or I for it. I will keep on a little and try a different door.
Danyal came to cut and has an open circle. I will look at his lodging.
Danyal came when called and his share is already paid. I will go and thank him; a visit moved the day last time.
Requested layout check, not my own wish: switching to phone size briefly.
Layout check interaction: opening About on the small screen.
Small screen: the map shrinks to a strip and the house row is cut at both edges, but text and buttons were readable. Back to my desktop size.
Danyal, a well keeper, friend of Maryam, thirty days here. The kind of detail I like. I sit with him and wait.
I have arrived but he says nothing yet. Back to the notebook.

So it did move: it is morning and ten have come, Maryam and the overseer among them. My want to leave eases; the patience paid. But Yusuf, who came on the first day with his own sickle, now postpones for his own barley. Same man, other answer. I notice that and I like noticing it, though I am guessing at the reason: the storm flattened his field.
Watching the day.
Twenty have come now without my insisting, and the list shrinks as I watch; that is the kind of slow change I enjoy, though one day took two real minutes when the first took fifteen seconds.
Letting the day run.
Still sitting at Danyal's, almost two minutes for a couple of hours. Let me see if the cutting shows in the ledger.

Here is a contradiction I cannot pass. The news said the storm flattened 108 measures in the landowner's field. The ledger still says about 250 uncut, the same as before the storm, and still says Rain is expected on 20 July, though it is the 21st and the storm came. Twenty people came and only about 5 are cut. Either the flattened barley is still counted or the ledger has not been written up. I do not trust the book now.
Back to the notebook.
Twenty-six came, only Dere holds back. Without one insisting word. Good. Now I want to see the field come down.
Walking back. 21 July has lasted three real minutes now.
Home. Twenty-seven of twenty-eight. Now the numbers.

Twenty cut, 230 standing. It moves, like a tram counter. At this pace the field will take most of my evening; I can watch it but there is little for me to do. The ledger line about rain on 20 July is still there.
What else can a steward order while they cut?

reaction: The ledger covers the orders; back first.
Now the other orders.

Write to the landowner is greyed: You can write when the estimate shows too little grain. But by my own sums 30 in the granary and 250 in the field never reach 384. So either the households' shares make up the rest, which I have not seen counted, or the estimate is something else. I am guessing. Both orders are closed; there is nothing to do but wait for the cutting.
Back to watch.
Watching. Nothing to decide.
The village is working and that is satisfying, but 21 July has lasted over five real minutes with no decision for me, while the first day took fifteen seconds.

I would leave now. The cutting goes on without me, both orders are closed, and the only thing left to press is Hold to insist for one Dere person, which I do not want to do. I will watch one more stretch to see whether the day turns.
One more stretch.
Still 21 July, nothing new. I am going to the menu to put it down.
Opening Feedback only to look. I will not write or send anything.
Both I'm stopping and I'm confused are here. I am stopping because nothing is left for me to do, not mainly from confusion, so I choose stopping. No text, no Submit.

I am stopping on 21 July with twenty-seven of twenty-eight at the landowner's barley and about 230 still standing. I liked the people answering in their own way and catching the overseer and Yusuf changing their answers. But after I called them there was nothing for me to decide, the day stood still for minutes, and the ledger still promised rain on a date already past. Pressing I'm stopping put those words into the note box by itself; I typed nothing and did not press Submit. I would not leave it running. I might come back another evening on the desktop to see the threshing and whether the households make up the hundred missing measures, but not tonight.
